stats.limits.title: Plan limits
stats.help.title: Server status
stats.help.intro: Server status shows how much CPU, memory, and disk capacity the machine running the console is using. It is a quick view for spotting sustained pressure before the experience becomes slow or unstable.
stats.help.first.title: First steps
stats.help.first.step1: Find CPU, RAM, and DSK in the right sidebar footer.
stats.help.first.step2: Read each bar's percentage and color; when the rail is collapsed, look at the fill of the icon rings.
stats.help.first.step3: Hover over the widget to see the hostname, used and total RAM, load, and uptime.
stats.help.first.step4: Pay attention to amber or red values that persist across several refreshes, not an isolated spike.
stats.help.legend.title: Legend
stats.help.legend.cpu.name: CPU
stats.help.legend.cpu.desc: processor workload percentage at that moment; a short spike can be normal
stats.help.legend.ram.name: RAM
stats.help.legend.ram.desc: memory actually occupied according to the system's available memory
stats.help.legend.disk.name: DSK
stats.help.legend.disk.desc: percentage of capacity used on the disk where the console lives
stats.help.legend.low.name: Below 60%
stats.help.legend.mid.name: 60% to 84%
stats.help.legend.mid.desc: worth watching if it persists or keeps rising
stats.help.legend.high.name: 85% or more
stats.help.legend.high.desc: high pressure; for disk, freeing space is especially urgent
stats.help.buttons.title: Buttons and actions
stats.help.buttons.hover.v: Shows supplementary host data. The widget has no buttons and runs no actions.
stats.help.warning.title: Watch out for this
stats.help.warning.text: These rings measure machine resources, not token consumption: that lives in Usage and tokens. A brief CPU spike is usually normal; watch for sustained red, RAM that does not drop, or disk nearing its limit.
